claims.text: The conventional EAM reference should be replaced by a neural-network or physics-informed multi-body interatomic potential trained on high-temperature ab initio data.
A high-temperature-trained multi-body ML potential will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch in both solid and liquid high-entropy alloys near melting.
Equimolar quinary metallic high-entropy alloys are a relevant class of multicomponent systems.
TOR-TILD EAM references inadequately represent the diverse ab initio configurations of these alloys, particularly in the liquid.
The intervention applies to equimolar or near-equimolar quinary high-entropy alloys at approximately 0.9 times their melting temperature.
The proposed potential is applicable to both solid and liquid phases.
High-entropy-alloy solids exhibit substantial configurational or packing disorder.
A flexible multi-body potential can account for many-body interactions and the extensive configurational diversity of a multicomponent alloy.
A DFT-trained deep-learning potential can accurately describe both solid and liquid high-entropy materials.
More accurate reproduction of solid and liquid configurations will enhance overlap between the reference and ab initio ensembles.
Enhanced phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to EAM references.
The intervention could reduce thermodynamic-integration error by about 50% in both solid and liquid states.
The benefit will be greatest for high-melting, near-equimolar high-entropy alloys.
The benefit may diminish for lower-melting or highly asymmetric compositions.
The magnitude of improvement depends on the quality of the multi-body potential's parameterization.
A controlled benchmark should compare EAM and ML references for the same equimolar quinary alloy, temperature, phases, and sampling protocol.
The benchmark will measure free-energy differences, convergence rates, phase-space overlap, and variation along the integration coordinate.
The hypothesis is falsified if the ML reference provides less than a 30% statistically significant improvement in path mismatch and does not improve convergence relative to EAM.
